cover.subtitle: Discussion document

slides.title: Year in review
slides.summary: Deal activity returned to pre-pandemic levels

slides.text: Dealmaking has returned to pre-pandemic levels, and the capital that stayed on the sidelines is coming back to fundamentals.
slides.subtext: Three findings from the year in review

slides.title: PE-VC activity declined by ~35% between 2022 and 2023, returning to pre-pandemic levels

points.text: as global macro headwinds, high interest rates and valuation mismatches slowed dealmaking
with deal value down ~60% as investors focused on unit economics
with a ~20% decline, supported by large buyouts in healthcare and energy

points.lead: Dry powder remains at a record
points.text: so deployment is set to recover as valuations settle

slides.title: Traditional sectors demonstrated resilience in an otherwise slowing market

exhibit.heading: Annual PE-VC investments in India by sector

points.text: over 2022–23 as cautionary investor sentiment hit business-model viability
as most scale assets were well funded post-2021 and valuation mismatches persisted
in 2023, gaining share as investors backed proven models

slides.title: South Korea limited spread through rapid cluster investigation and scaled testing

exhibit.heading: Incremental cases per day in South Korea

points.text: after 16 reported cases, with 180,000 individuals tested by Mar 9
as Daegu residents cleared streets and the church congregation was traced
as localised outbreaks continued past the peak
from a 909-case peak on Feb 29 to under 100 by Mar 20, without a national lockdown

slides.soWhat: Testing capacity and contact tracing, not movement restrictions, did the work in the first wave.

slides.title: Washington DC ranks third among very large US urban areas for congestion delay

callout.text: 102 hours of yearly delay per auto commuter and $2,015 of congestion cost; excess fuel follows the same ranking

slides.title: Sector outlook: healthcare and manufacturing stay strong while IT stays soft

rows: Multi-specialty and single-specialty provider platforms; scale assets attracting buyouts
China+1 tailwinds, PLI incentives, EV supply chain
NBFC and fintech consolidation at reset valuations

callout.text: ↑ strong activity expected; → moderate; ↓ limited activity

slides.soWhat: Healthcare and advanced manufacturing carry the 2024 pipeline; IT services need a valuation reset before deal flow returns.
slides.note: Outlook reflects Bain's deal-team view of 2024 activity, not a forecast of returns

slides.title: Retail and corporate banking hold two thirds of the revenue pool, mostly domestic

exhibit.heading: Banking revenue pool by business line and geography, 2025

points.text: so rate and deposit dynamics at home drive the largest pool
with two thirds of revenue booked in Europe and Asia

points.lead: Payments is small but growing fastest
points.text: and skews to Asia

slides.title: Transit commutes track income and place of work across the District's wards

series.name: Commute by public transportation, % of commuters
Place of work outside DC, % of workers

points: Wards 7 and 8 combine the highest transit share with the lowest incomes
A third of their workers commute outside the District, where high-frequency service is thin
Improving cross-boundary transit reaches the riders who depend on it most

slides.title: Survey
slides.summary: GenAI use cases in credit are moving from pilot to deployment

slides.title: Institutions prioritise productivity improvement when initiating GenAI use cases

kpi.label: of institutions rank productivity improvement first

points.text: for 44% of institutions, ahead of compliance in every region except the EU
for 25%, concentrated among the banks already inside supervisory GenAI reviews
for 50%, which is what a pilot portfolio looks like before it reaches production

slides.soWhat: Productivity is the stated case, so the first production use cases will be judged on analyst time saved, not on revenue.

slides.title: Most institutions have access to external GenAI tools but half require internal guidelines first

metrics.label: have access to external GenAI solutions
have no access to these tools

points: Access is broad but governed: most institutions gate use behind guideline training
Data-security training is the second most common prerequisite
The few without access cite regulatory uncertainty

slides.title: Investment themes: a return to fundamentals across sectors and geographies

points.text: and gained share, with ~75% of investments in 2023 against ~60% in 2022
of ~$5.5 billion in 2023, driven by a threefold increase in provider deal value

points.lead: IT/ITeS deal activity continued to taper
points.text: declining by ~65% as valuations reset and end markets normalised
on supply chain diversification, government incentives and scale assets

Combine traditional improvement levers with an end-to-end digital transformation
